method: 7 built-in image calls; 8 authored Remotion studies
notes: 02b is the selected architecture revision; 02 retained as an earlier attempt.
05 and 06 are code-native SVG overlays over source 01.
Synthetic chart values; no factual claims.
No AI image-to-video generation was used. No scene layer segmentation.
Original PNGs copied without pixel editing.

assets.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset: a wide 16:9 painted scenery plate for Parallax, without people.
Scene: a calm river bend crossed by one modest stone footbridge. The water comes from the distant center-left toward the lower-right foreground. A low walnut bank curves in from the lower left; a few grouped dark reeds mark the near edge. The footbridge occupies the middle distance, connecting the two banks. One small cluster of quiet rectangular buildings sits far beyond it. The upper half is mostly open bone-colored daylight.
Medium: mature editorial gouache with constructivist composition, broad unequal opaque planes, visible selected brush edges and calm intervals. Use restrained ink, walnut, bone, ochre and a little muted blue-gray water. Let architecture and banks have clear silhouettes, with a few observed details at the bridge. Group vegetation into masses.
Keep the water surface and sky spacious. Paper tooth is subtle, not an all-over pattern. Believable bridge, shore and water geometry; no fantasy glow, photography, glossy 3D rendering, triangulated surface mesh, tiny decorative flecks, figures, text, labels or borders.

Use case: style-transfer.
Image 1 is the scene and composition reference. Reinterpret the same river crossing as a painted architectural stage set for Parallax.
Keep the river's route, footbridge position, bank silhouettes, distant building group and camera. Translate the banks into a few clean interlocking stage planes. Simplify the bridge into a long restrained ochre slab with three readable rectangular piers reaching to the river bed; its walkway connects both banks. Give the buildings broad ink and walnut faces with one decisive long shadow. Use flat gouache edges, generous bone daylight and a few hand-drawn construction contours. The scene should feel like a deliberately assembled architectural theatre, with one shared perspective and clear support.
Remove scattered reeds, tiny foliage marks and most naturalistic surface detail. Retain painted warmth and selected edges; no miniature toy rendering, glossy 3D, photo texture, repeating triangular facets, decorative debris, humans, text or panels.

Use case: style-transfer.
Image 1 is a composition reference for the river crossing. Completely repaint it as an austere hand-painted architectural theatre. Preserve only the river route, central bridge, distant right-hand building group and low camera position. Replace the large left tree with a single dark upright rectangular stage wing. Reduce the right buildings to four plain ochre cuboids with no roofs or windows. Make the bridge one straight bone-colored slab resting visibly on three rectangular walnut piers. Replace the banks with four large interlocking ochre and walnut planes; every plane has one flat painted tone. Water is one broad muted blue-gray shape with only two quiet horizontal brush strokes. Sky is a blank warm bone field. Add one crisp long shadow from the stage wing across the near bank.
Use deliberately economical gouache, broad opaque strokes and selected uneven edges. Keep one coherent perspective and physically supported bridge. This is a spare surreal stage for an editorial film. Remove all foliage, masonry, rippling reflections and small descriptive marks. No all-over mottling, canvas texture, tiny chips, facets, photorealism, gradient lighting, miniature render, text, people or decorative debris.

Use case: illustration-story.
Asset: one isolated painted object on a genuinely transparent background, for independent animation in Parallax.
Subject: a single small ceramic teacup, viewed slightly from above in three-quarter view. A round open rim, an oval dark interior, a thick ochre body tapering gently toward a stable foot, and one simple loop handle at the right. Its rim, inner opening, foot and handle have coherent ceramic geometry. No saucer or other objects.
Medium: mature editorial gouache, matte opaque ochre, bone highlights and walnut/ink shadow planes. Model its volume with a few unequal broad planes and two or three selected brush-edge details. Make the cup feel observed and hand painted, with subtle asymmetry, rather than a perfect icon or a photorealistic product shot. Plain surface, no logo, writing, pattern or ornament.
Center the full cup with generous transparent margin. No ground plane, cast shadow, backdrop, checkerboard drawn into the image, glossy glaze, reflections or 3D render finish.

Use case: stylized-concept.
Image 1 is the object identity and medium reference: the ochre teacup. Make a second isolated painted object on a genuinely transparent background.
Turn this same cup into a small surreal architectural cutaway. Retain its overall ochre cup silhouette, oval open top, stable foot and single right loop handle. Remove a broad front section of the wall to expose an empty circular interior floor, one short stair along the inner left wall and a simple upper landing. Treat the cup wall as a thick ceramic architectural shell, with clearly drawn cut edges. Keep stairs and landing inside the cup and coherent in the same three-quarter perspective. This is an intentional impossible object, not a factual diagram of a teacup.
Use the same mature matte gouache and unequal ochre/bone/walnut planes, a few selected hand-drawn contours and quiet surface detail. Center the whole object with transparent margins. No people, furniture, landscape, ground, cast shadow, photorealism, glossy 3D, text, labels or extra handles.

Use case: productivity-visual.
Asset: a wide 16:9 painted backdrop beneath a Remotion chart. Paint the background only; no chart or text.
Create a bone-paper field with a very restrained architectural impression at its outer edges: one broad pale walnut vertical plane along the far left edge, one muted ochre patch near the upper-right corner, and a faint hand-painted shadow band near the bottom. The central 75 percent of the image remains almost uniform light bone, including a large quiet horizontal region for small chart labels.
Mature editorial gouache with calm asymmetry, subtle dry-brush boundaries and barely visible paper tooth. A few broad shapes, no focal object. Keep all contrast and texture weak enough to sit behind dark typography. No gradients suggesting a spotlight, frame, distressed stains, speckles, triangles, grid, decorative squiggles, handwriting, letters, numbers or diagram.

Use case: lighting-weather.
Image 1 is the edit target: the light painted chart backdrop. Make its dark companion using the same broad peripheral arrangement and quiet central region.
Repaint the field in deep matte ink and walnut. Keep the center uniformly dark with extremely subtle tonal variation. Translate the far-left plane into slightly lighter walnut, the upper-right patch into a subdued umber plane, and the lower shadow band into deeper ink. Keep edges visible only through gentle tonal differences. The central 75 percent is reserved for pale chart lines and labels and has no high-contrast marks.
Retain mature hand-painted gouache edges and very restrained paper tooth. No chart, text, numbers, objects, star field, noisy grain, glowing gradients, smoke, vignette spotlight, metallic highlights or borders.

studies.title: Quiet painted landscape
studies.motion: A restrained push and pan across one painting.
studies.verdict: Warm and readable, but pastoral and familiar. The foliage and stonework are busier than intended.

studies.title: Architectural theatre
studies.motion: The same push and pan across simplified planes.
studies.verdict: A stronger graphic alternative. The revised version removes foliage and descriptive buildings; the spare stage carries the identity.
studies.use: Abstract systems, distance and institutional scale.

studies.title: Observed object
studies.motion: A transparent cup settles above an authored contact shadow.
studies.verdict: A useful grounding asset with a coherent rim and handle. The tactile surface is more realistic than our flatter character language.
studies.use: Care, routines, gifts and material value.

studies.title: An impossible interior
studies.motion: The same entrance and subtle whole-object drift.
studies.verdict: The most distinctive metaphor here. A cup becomes a small architectural interior; use selectively so the surprise retains meaning.
studies.use: Inner worlds, hidden structure and conceptual reveals.

studies.title: Drawn analysis
studies.motion: A bridge contour, leader and near-bank label draw in.
studies.verdict: A strong bridge between painterly scenes and explanation. Keep marks anchored to what the narration is discussing.

studies.title: Theatrical foreground
studies.motion: Foreground wings open slightly; a pale diagonal wash changes gently.
studies.verdict: Adds framing and depth, but can feel imposed. This is an occasional theatrical device; the analytical version is more useful day to day.
studies.use: Thresholds, a framed point of view and chapter atmosphere.

studies.title: Light painted field
studies.motion: Chart structure, bars and terminal values appear in sequence.
studies.verdict: The most reusable treatment. The painted edges add warmth while the quiet middle keeps labels readable.

studies.title: Dark painted field
studies.motion: The exact same chart sequence, with pale text and neutral bars.
studies.verdict: A coherent dark companion. The surface is still fairly textured; a quieter version may be better for dense graphics.
studies.use: Serious turns, contrast and sparse analytical sequences.
